newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee market dulled by absence of roasters.
newsitem.headline: German coffee market dulled by absence of roasters.

text.p: German coffee roasters are sidelined in the physical market because they have adequate April-June cover and retail sales are slack, traders said on Monday.
"The industry is not interested in outright purchases right now -- recent green coffee orders are arriving and, while the pace of roastings is active, ex-plants sales are slow," one said.
"Most buyers are concentrating on May/July switches in New York arabicas, where origin price fixings are prevalent."
Consumers were waiting for futures prices to fall and believed coffee might not be as tight as in recent months.
Traders said they were wary of such an attitude.
The industry was also preoccupied with implementing retail price increases announced in February.
In a competitive market, prices for identical roasted coffees sometimes still differed by 3.50 marks per 0.5 kg.
Importers reported outright purchases of Brazils and East African spot arabicas as well as some robustas.
They noted an increase in availability of spot milds, but said offers for the second half of 1997 were not forthcoming.
Brazils were at $207 per 50 kg fob April, with May/June at $195. Colombians were not available for April while May/June was offered at $237.
Vietnam robustas grade 2 cost $72.50 cif for April and $72 May/June.
